chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: Forming the Callender trio and returning to the Los Angeles recording scene
summary: He forms a King Cole style trio with Sir Charles Thompson and Louis Gonsales, books through William Morris, and later returns to LA to record with many leaders.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: That was '44 or '45, somewhere in there. I signed up with the William Morris Agency, and they booked my little trio. We worked upstate New York through Ohio, and all kind of crazy little gigs. We'd play our little music and sing songs, you know. I guess everybody tried to emulate King Cole at the time, and we were no exception.
Well, I don't consider myself a singer, but I can carry a tune. [LAUGHS]
I would guess that you probably could.

So all during this period I wasn't playing my tuba at all, because, you know, it was enough hassle carrying the bass around. I don't think I picked the tuba up again until some years later. Matter of fact, yeah, I picked the tuba up after I had gone to... I'm jumping around again.

So the trio went on for a while. Then I came back to Los Angeles and I really got deeply into the recording scene, and that's how I guess I managed to record with so many people -- Wardell Gray, Dexter Gordon, Charlie Parker, Erroll Garner and Bumps Myers.
